items.title: Taking a Chinese kitchen-equipment maker into the Philippines
items.sub: A factory that already exports most of what it makes wanted its own brand in the Philippines: one published price, a sales team, dealers and a service network, ready for a launch season. This is what we prepared.

did.t: A market study from public data
did.d: Demand sized from outlets by format, hotels and their pipeline, and customs import records by tariff line, with a low, base and high case. Every figure carries its source and the date it was read.
Each competitor's range, channels, published prices, warranty and service, read from official sites and authorised retailers, to find the position nobody holds.

did.t: A position, a price ladder and a name
did.d: One position with three proofs (quality, price and after-sales), entry, core and premium prices by category, and one brand name cleared and filed as a trademark before launch.

did.t: A range made for the Philippines
did.d: Launch models chosen from the factory catalogue and specified for Philippine power, humid and salty kitchens and tropical heat, with local plugs, English manuals and the safety reports customs asks for.
Our Philippine entity imports: customs accreditation, a standards confirmation for each model, a tariff ruling and the ASEAN–China duty preference.
Door-to-door sea and air freight from China, containers ordered against confirmed demand, and buffer stock staged before typhoon season.
A local warranty written to Philippine consumer law, service hubs opened city by city, spare parts held in Manila, a named technician on every invoice and QR registration on every unit.

A direct sales team, regional dealers with territories and demo stock, projects with hotels, chains and franchisors, and online stores. One published price everywhere, and clear rules so channels never undercut each other.
Every large city and municipality ranked into tiers, each with its own coverage: the direct team, dealers or online. A tier opens only when the one before it has passed its gate.
A local website with the price list and chat, marketplace stores, a showroom with a test kitchen, short videos every week in Taglish, and the country's main foodservice trade shows.
Trade shows, performance ads, content, a demo fleet, dealer programmes and PR, budgeted low, medium and high, and part-funded by the factory.

did.t: The team, the model and the scorecard
did.d: The local team and premises, and one working model behind every number: a monthly build by channel, profit and loss, break-even, funding, a downside case, a risk register and a quarterly scorecard with guardrails.

phases.d: One city, the first container, and pilot installs with founding customers. The name, trademark, price list, website and online stores are built.
phases.gate: Pilots installed and the next orders booked.

phases.d: A trade-show launch before the hot season, the greater capital region, the first dealers, service in the next two cities, and the projects channel opens.
phases.gate: Units sold, dealers signed and the first customer stories published.

phases.d: Regional capitals, the full dealer network, more service hubs, the wider catalogue and the online push.
